and i'm using mysql just in case =).. but i guess it's not important
that is completely important because mysql uses positional parameters.

> that is completely important because mysql uses positional parameters.

sorry =)
it's just, mysql and sqlite have no ARRAY datatype so there is no case where there would be a list passed as a bound parameter.

so...I'm still guessing.  you are relying on the mysql driver expanding out a list into a set of IN parameters ? because that doesn't normally work that way.   there's a way it can work in all cases but that's not what you're doing there.

in my case it still works..
so will wait until the next problem or will forget about sqlalchemy and live without it like before

thanx for consultation =)
it's an issue i just needed to know enough context

rename.to: guessing of parameter style fails for positional params plus array parameter

rename.from: guessing of parameter style fails for positional params plus array parameter
rename.to: guessing of parameter style in logging / exceptions fails for positional params plus array parameter

body:
**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**pass executemany context to _repr_params** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1508

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**pass executemany context to _repr_params** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1509

what it's doing is being passed whether or not the query is an "executemany" or not from the outside.  since this is not always known, it still does the "guess" if executemany wasn't passed in, but ideally it would always be passed in and that whole guessing logic can be removed.     once it knows true/false for that, then it can repr appropriately.   your test case is one where it detects "executemany" style when it's not.
i might make the change more aggressive in 1.4.  for 1.3 just looking to not break things
all of the guessing in that code turns out to be silly, if you run the parameters through trunc() without determining anything about them it looks 99% the same as if we did all the checking.
